caseno: Appeal From Original Order (FMA) No. 147 of 2005 with Civil Rule No. 335 (FM) of 2005
lawyer:
Dr M Zahir with M Hassan, Advocates—For the Appellants. 
TH Khan with Waliur Reza Choudhury, Advocates—For Respondent No. 1. 
Salahuddin with Ramjan Ali Sikder, Abu Khaled Al-Mamun, Advocates—For the Added Respondent No. 4
parties:
Adel Miah (Md) and another ------ Appellants 
Vs 
 Shajeeb Corporation and others ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
2. The defendants are appellants of Miscellaneous appeal. The respondent No. 1, as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 15 of 2005 in the court of District Judge, Dhaka, for permanent as well as mandatory injunction against infringement of registered Trade Mark. In the plaint the plaintiff sought for a decree of permanent injunction restraining the defendants Nos. 1 and 2 and anybody claiming through or under them from imitating or infringing the registered trade mark of the plaintiff's soft drinks powder brand 'Tang', as shown in Schedule A to the plaint and also from producing, manufacturing, selling of said soft drink powder using infringed trade mark under the name 'Spry Tang' as shown in Schedule B to the plaint, on the plea of trade mark similar to and resembling or identical with the plaintiff's registered trade mark Schedule 'A' in any manner and for a decree in the form of mandatory injunction directing the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 to withdraw and take back all soft drink products under their infringed and fictitious and copied trade mark 'Spry Tang' from the market immediately and to destroy them publicly and in the manner to the satisfaction of the plaintiff by filing an application under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure prayed for a temporary injunction. Plaintiff stated that the plaintiff is a proprietary business concern engaged in import and export of merchandise and also dealing in other trading business, commission agent, and also as distributor of soft drink bearing Trade name 'Tang' distributing the products since long, with their business office as given in the cause Title of the plaint and thereby have created goodwill in the market. Messrs Craft USA is the producer, manufacturer and seller of food product under the name and style Craft Family, who obtained certificate of Registration on 2nd July, 1987 under Trade Mark Registration No. 25566 in Class 32 with their trade name "Tang'. The trade licence number of the plaintiff is 14975 dated 18th January 2005. The BSTI issued certificate in favour of manufacturer vide No. 6089/1-5-2005 dated 5th February, 2005. The product under trade name Tang has become so popular in Bangladesh. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 using a different trades name has been marketing soft drink product under the plaintiff's trade mark 'Tang' by adding a word 'Spry' on the left side of the name 'Tang' with very small letters, hardly visible from even short distance, keeping all the other contents of the plaintiff's trade mark 'Tang' unchanged, which is hardly distinguishable. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 for doing so has not yet got any trade mark. They are manufacturing and marketing their illegal products throughout the country and in the meantime, thousands of customers have been cheated. Thus, they have been infringing the trade mark of the plaintiff. 

 3. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the injunction petition by filing a joint written objection denying all the material allegations made against them in the petition and contended that the defendant No. 1 obtained design registration from the Department of Pa tents, Designs and Trade Marks, in accordance with the Patents and Design Act in relation both to the glass container and hard packet of 'Spry Tang'. The plaintiff has got no design registration of the shape, get-up and the containers and, as such, the allegation of imitation against the principal defendants is baseless. It was further stated that the investment in new places has always been encouraged in an economically backward country like Bangladesh. The defendant has done everything required to do by law in order to start a business. He obtained the city corporation trade licence and certificates from BSTI, Design Registration from the Department of Patents, Designs and Trade Mark, and has applied for Registration of Trade Mark of his product which is pending before the Trade Mark Registration office. It was stated that the plaintiff lodged a criminal case under sections 420/486/487 of the Penal Code in the Kotwali Police Station. Comilla on 1-6-2004, alleging that the defendant No. 1 was deceiving the customers by using the name and counterfeit trade mark of 'Tang' upon his goods. The defendant No. 1 brought a Miscellaneous case in High Court Division under section 561A of the CrPC for quashment of the said proceedings and a Bench of this Court by order dated 9-8-2004 observed that the defendant No. 1 has been producing and marketing his soft drink powder after obtaining due licence from BSTI and design registration. The defendant prayed for rejection of the injunction petition. The District Judge after hearing both the parties allowed the petition for temporary injunction on contest against defendant Nos. 1 and 2, restraining them from manufacturing, selling, distributing and marketing soft drinks under the trade name 'Spry Tang' till disposal of the suit. From the said order the defendants above preferred this appeal. 

 5. Dr Mr Zahir, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the appellant, submits that the appellant No. 1 is Adel Mia, proprietor of ATN Food and Consumer Product and defendant No. 1, got his Trade licence on 4-9-2004 from Tongi Pourashava, Gazipur, for carrying on business of powder drinks and other food and consumer products and the defendant No. 2 is a concern of Md Adel Mia, which, also got trade licence on 4-9-2004 from Tongi Pourashava for carrying on business of other agricultural products. He submits that plaintiff got Trade licence from Dhaka City Corporation on 18-1-2005, and got the testing certificate from BSTI on 5-2-2005 giving effect from 1-8-2004 which was valid up to 30-6-2005, and he submits that the defendant got trade licence on 4-9-2004 and BSTI certificate on 5-2-2005 and the defendant is a prior user of the Trade Mark in the market and the plaintiff who got licence and BSTI certificate after the defendant cannot restrain the defendant in using the trade mark. In support of his submission, he refers to the case of Kohinoor Chemical Co Bangladesh Ltd vs Kohinoor Chemical Co Ltd reported in 48 DLR 376. 

 6. Mr TH Khan, learned Senior Advocate appearing for the respondents, submits that Trade Mark 'Tang' was registered on 2nd July 1987 in the name of Craft General Foods Inc of USA which mark has been renewed up to date and the same is valid. The plaintiff is the sole distributor for Bangladesh for the products of the Craft USA and was authorised to franchise for making and doing work with Government of Bangladesh, and accordingly, the plaintiff has been in the market as distributor of the products under the Trade Mark 'Tang' long before. He submits that there is no registration of Trade Mark in favour of the defendant, and from the written objection it appears that they have only applied for registration. Whereas, the plaintiff getting Trade Mark registration in 1987 has been marketing the products under trade mark through import. The defendant only got design registration for the bottles and hard paper packet on 1-4-2004 for 'Spry Tang' for pre-servation of natural fresh orange flavour drinks mix 'Spry Tang' and he submits that there is no registration of Trade Mark for the products of the defendant No. 1. The learned trial Court found that the defendant got a certificate from BSTI in the name of 'Spry' and got design registration from Patents and Design and Trade Mark Department for bottles and packet and the defendant got certificate from BSTI in the name of Spry, and found that defendants were marketing their products in the name of 'Spry Tang' for which they had no licence or Trade Mark and the trial Court finding prima facie case rightly granted injunction in favour of the plaintiff. 

 7. The added respondent No. 4 filed an affidavit-in-opposition against the Rule and stated that Craft Foods Holding is the exclusive and beneficial owner of the Trade Mark. The Trade Mark 'Tang' No. 25566 dated 2-7-1987 was initially registered in the name of Craft General Foods, which name was subsequently changed to Craft Foods Inc on 5th April 2000. The Registrar of Trade Marks, Government of Bangladesh, issued a renewal Certificate dated 4-10-2003 in the name of added respondent Kraft Foods Holding Inc who is the lawful owner of the Trade Mark 'Tang' bearing Registration No. 25566 dated 2-7-1987 under the licence agreement with Kraft Foods International Inc. It has the right to manufacture, advertise, promote, distribute and sell, powdered beverage under the mark 'Tang' in Bangladesh. The orange beverage product bearing the said Trade Mark 'Tang' and Tang Plus are internationally reputed products and are sold widely in Bangladesh through distributors. The product has been widely sold previously through different importers from Singapore to Bangladesh. An impersonator named "Kraft General Foods Inc of Sea-2-2 Handily Road, Singapore had filed application seeking registration of mark bearing 'Tang'. There was an objection by the respondent. Ultimately, objections were maintained and the applications of the impersonator were abandoned. It has been stated that the defendant No. 1 was in collusion with the impersonator of the name of Kraft General Food and he has been engaged in fraudulent practice by selling and marketing their product by adding words Spry before the word 'Tang' which is hardly visible even from short distance, and thus often escapes the eye of an unwary innocent customer and the potential customers of the added respondent's products are deceived and misled. The label so adapted is also similar and identical to that of the label design of added respondent, including the colour. It has been stated that the defendant got a certificate from BSTI for preserving and marketing of soft drink powder bearing mark Spry only. But obtaining such a certificate of registration, defendant No. 1 fraudulently started marketing products in the name of 'Spry Tang' without permission from BSTI. Lastly, it has been stated that the defendant failed to come to the court with clean hands, which disentitles them from getting any relief as prayed for as they adopted a deceitful mark imitating added respondent's registered trade mark 'Tang' by way of adding 'Spry'. The added respondent being the owner of the Trade Mark 'Tang' supported the case of the plaintiff-appellant as their distributor in Bangladesh. 

 8. Mr Salahuddin, learned Senior Counsel appearing in the hearing with Mr Sk Ramjan Ali Sikdar and Mr Khalid Al Mamun for the added respondent No. 4, supported the case of plaintiff appellant and submitted that the Trade Mark 'Tang' has been in use in the country by import for long time having registration with Trade Mark. The plaintiff has been using the trade mark as sole distributor under them in Bangladesh. Whereas the defendants have no Trade Mark Registration, but only got patent design for preservation of the powder mix and he cited case of Rexona Properetary Ltd vs Majid Soap reported in PLD 1956 Sind Universal Pharmaceutical Ltd vs Social Marketing Company Ltd reported in 2 MLR (AD) 200, Sunil Kumar Das vs Canon Kubushi and another, reported in 57 DLR 93, Abdul Jabbar vs Ahmed Jan PLD 1973 Karachi 289 in support of his submission and to repel the submission of the learned Advocate for the appellant. 

 9. I have heard the learned Advocates of both sides. Perused the memo of appeal, the papers filed with application for vacating the order of stay, counter-affidavits and reply. It appears from the application for stay of operation of impugned judgment and decree filed by the appellant that by the certificate of Registration of Trade Mark No. 25566, the Trade Mark 'Tang' was registered on 2nd July 1987 and was renewed on 4-10-2003 in favour of the respondent No. 4. The plaintiff got BSTI certificate for soft drink powder on 1-8-2004 for Trade Mark Tang'. The defendant got registration of design for bottles for preservation of 'Spry Tang', natural fresh orange flavour instant drink mix vide registration No. 05903 dated 11-1-2004 on 2-4-2004 and the certificate was issued on 24-4-2004. While the registration of design for packet of hard paper was granted vide design No. 05977 dated 22-3-2004 on 28-6-2004 and it was issued on 28-6-2004. It appears that the added respondent No. 4 is the owner of the Trade Mark 'Tang' and that the plaintiff is a distributor for 'Tang'. Dr Zahir submitted that the plaintiff is neither owner or an user of the Trade Mark 'Tang' and plaintiffs has no locus standi to bring the suit for infringement of trade mark. But from perusal of the plaint, it appears that plaintiff asserted that they are distributor for the product of Trade Mark 'Tang' and other products of Kraft Family, The Annexure A to the application for injunction shows that the plaintiff is distributor and they were given franchise to take steps necessary with the government. The original owner of the Trade Mark 'Tang' is the respondent No. 4, who has supported the case of the plaintiff in the appeal. I find that the plaintiff has locus standi to sue the defendant against infringement of Trade Mark 'Tang'. Dr Zahir submitted next that the defendant has been a prior user of the Trade Mark in the country, as they got trade licence and the BSTI certificate earlier to the plaintiff and they are in the use of the trade mark and the defendants cannot be restrained by the plaintiff in the suit as framed and referred to the case of Kohinoor Chemical Bangladesh Ltd vs Kohinoor Chemical Ltd reported in 48 DLR 376. It appears that the defendant got only registration for patent and design for bottles and packets for preservation of 'Spry Tang', the CM licence was granted on 20-4-2004 for the soft drink powder Brand 'Spry', the defendants were found marketing their product under 'Spry Tang' without any Registration of Trade Mark and BSTI certificate. The learned District Judge finding the defendants were marketing their product in the name of Spry Tang without having registration granted injunction in favour of the plaintiff. There is prima facie and arguable case for the plaintiff and the trial Court did not commit any wrong in granting injunction. The question of determination of the prior use of the trade mark can only he gone into by evidence during trial of the suit. Thus, I find that there is no illegality in the impugned judgment. Further, the submission of the learned Advocate for the appellant that the investment in economically backward country like Bangladesh is to be encouraged does not seem encouraging to me in the facts of the case and the situation of rampant adulteration of food prevailing in the country.
